## During the seminar

Congressional elections and ultimatum-game data provide examples of selecting
columns, filtering and sorting rows, creating variables with `mutate()`,
and summarizing groups. We distinguish missing values from zeros and explore
lower and upper bounds for missing minimum acceptable offers.

We then practice working with text, reshaping tables, combining rows, and
joining datasets. Join audits check whether keys are unique, whether rows
were unexpectedly duplicated, and whether any records failed to match.
The demo includes frozen teaching datasets and source documentation, so no
in-class data downloads are required.

## After class

**A5 is due October 28 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** Accept your private repository
invitation and follow its README. Complete `R/a5_answers.R` and the QMD's
three short written responses. Save, run `Rscript checks/check-a5.R` in the
Terminal, and render a fresh HTML. Commit and push **the answers R file,
QMD, and current HTML**, then check GitHub Actions.

Keep track of what each row represents before and after a transformation.
In particular, counting rows is not always the same as summing the counts
stored in a column.
